pr_body:
Fixes #8352.

This allows additional cops to be run before the current one, allowing us to test interactions between cops more effectively.

cc: @marcandre 

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [x] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [ ] Added tests.
* [x] Added an entry to the [Changelog](https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format).
* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Run `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and RuboCop for itself, and generates the documentation.
pr_comments: Just pushing this immediately for now to get feedback on the approach.

Cool!

First question is: order should not matter, so it shouldn't be "run first", simply "also run". We already have `other_cops` for extra config. One thing I was curious is: if we add the cops of these config to the running cops, will this create issue with the current test suite? Because if not, that would probably be a good starting point. Maybe `let(:other_cop_classes) { other_cops.each_key{ |cop_name| # get the cop }`, which could be overwritten. What do you think?

Thanks for giving it a look!

You'd think order doesn't matter, but unfortunately that's not true. In the original issue I was looking at fixing, running the cops in the opposite order actually did not surface the bug. That's because if you insert spaces and then a colon, everything is fine; inserting a colon and then spaces causes the break.

The approach of using `other_cops` is a good one - didn't think of doing it backwards that way :) Will give that a go! I'll rerun the suite and see if it causes any failures.

@marcandre bad news - this causes 47 failures in the current test suite. :( Right now the config is basically set so that the cop under test can *check* settings, but the *output* expects only that one cop to be run (so the other cops are catching issues that this cop doesn't care about).

Thanks for checking about `other_cops`.

The ordering thing bothers me tbh.

I'm wondering if another approach wouldn't be better, something like...

```ruby
expect_offense(<<~RUBY, cop_class: FirstCopClass)
 # ...
expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
  # intermediate stage
expect_offense(<<~RUBY)
  # ...
expect_correction(<<~RUBY)
  # final stage
```

I realize that you can't override `cop_class` or similar at the `expect_offense` level but that's something I was thinking would be cool to have.
That's definitely a neat idea. More specifically, instead of relying on `cop_class`, rewriting it to allow you to pass in a cop to the things you're expecting. I can look at that approach as well.

What I had in mind is:
```ruby
  let(:cop) do
    cop_class.new(config, cop_options).tap do |cop|
      cop.send :begin_investigation, processed_source
    end
  end
# become
  def cop(cop_class: cop_class, cop_options: cop_options, config: config, source: source, processed_source: processed_source(source))
    # ...
  end
```

TBH, the fact that `cop` depends does the `begin_investigation` is kind of a problem and should not be necessary, so this complicates things...

It might become too big too fast though

Hmm... I'm experimenting with the approach you mentioned above (using intermediate steps) and the problem is that the cops need to be part of the same rewriter in order to expose the bug. If you get the source out of the corrector and then pass it into the next cop, the bug won't happen. :( You really need to pass in both cops at the same time.
Oh wow, ok. So I guess the full CLI is a good regression test 🤷‍♂️

In this case, yep. The other method would be using the `run_first_cops` method which is currently in this PR. Not super clean but at least possible without running through the entire test suite. I'm OK either way.
@marcandre How are we proceeding here? I'm not very interested in this change, so I'll defer the decision on how to proceed to you.

I re-read this. The code is fine, I'm just not 100% we need it. The last bad interaction between cops we've had that I can recall is the one I created with the `#{ '  ' }` autocorrection, and this would not have helped, and wasn't necessary for testing.

So I'll close this for now and we can resurrect it if the need arises again.

issue_context.title: shared_context should allow for multiple cops
issue_context.body: There's no easy way to test interactions between multiple cops' autocorrections currently.
comments: I can push my PR for #8351 and repurpose it for this instead, since I got it working there.
Not as clearly needed as I thought. Closing for now.

Also: I can't recall when I tweaked how the correctors are merged, but it might be more difficult to create issues that need to happen at the same time. Should be ever more true whenever I manage to [tweak the `TreeRewriter` to improve conflicts detection](https://github.com/whitequark/parser/pull/727).

review_comments: I'm not sure why there's a `first` there. All correctors should be merged, I think `correctors.compact.inject(:merge!)` should work, and that method should be added to `InvestigationReport`
Not sure I 100% understand how you'd like this to look, but I'll give it a go and you'll let me know if I did it wrong. 😛
